rows.stem:
In the following experimental setup of electrolysis of water, if P and Q are the gases collected in the test tubes enclosing the electrodes R and S, then select the option/options in which the matching is correct :

(i) P – Oxygen gas , R – Anode

(ii) P – Hydrogen gas , R – Cathode

(iii) Q – Hydrogen gas , S – Cathode

(iv) Q – Oxygen gas , S – Anode
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the electrolysis setup (a jug of water, two test tubes P and Q inverted over electrodes R and S, wired to a battery) is given only as a drawing; which tube holds more gas, the one fact the matching turns on, is withheld here. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
In the electrolysis of water, the volume of hydrogen collected is twice that of oxygen. Hydrogen is given off at the cathode (negative electrode) and oxygen at the anode (positive electrode).

In the set-up, tube Q collects the larger volume of gas, so Q is hydrogen over the cathode S, and P is oxygen over the anode R. So (i) and (iii) are correct.

This is option (C) (i) and (iii).

rows.stem:
You have three aqueous solutions A, B and C as given below :

A - Potassium nitrate

B - Ammonium chloride

C - Sodium carbonate

The ascending order of the pH of these solutions is :
rows.solution:
Ammonium chloride is the salt of a strong acid and a weak base, so its solution is acidic (pH below 7). Potassium nitrate is the salt of a strong acid and a strong base, so its solution is neutral (pH 7). Sodium carbonate is the salt of a weak acid and a strong base, so its solution is basic (pH above 7).

The ascending order is B < A < C, which is option (D) B < A < C.

rows.stem: Select from the following a statement which is *not true* about burning of magnesium ribbon in air :

options.label: A
options.text: It burns with a dazzling white flame.

options.label: B
options.text: A white powder is formed on burning.

options.label: D
options.text: It is an example of a combination reaction.

rows.solution:
Burning magnesium gives out heat and light, so it is an exothermic reaction. The other statements are true: it burns with a dazzling white flame, a white powder (magnesium oxide) forms, and two substances combine into one.

The statement that is not true is option (C) It is an endothermic reaction.

rows.stem: A Hydrocarbon which **does not** belong to the same homologous series of carbon compounds is
rows.solution:
\(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\), \(\mathrm{C_6H_{14}}\) and \(\mathrm{C_{10}H_{22}}\) all fit \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}\), the general formula of the alkanes. \(\mathrm{C_7H_{14}}\) fits \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}\), the alkenes.

This is option (C) \(\mathrm{C_7H_{14}}\).

rows.stem: The colour of the solution observed after about 1 hour of placing iron nails in copper sulphate solution is
rows.solution:
Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulphate:

\(\mathrm{Fe(s) + CuSO_4(aq) \rightarrow FeSO_4(aq) + Cu(s)}\)

The blue solution turns pale green as iron(II) sulphate forms. This is option (B) Pale green.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: Juice of tamarind turns blue litmus to red. It is because of the presence of a chemical compound called
rows.solution:
Tamarind contains tartaric acid. (Acetic acid is in vinegar, methanoic acid in ant and nettle stings, and oxalic acid in tomato.)

This is option (D) Tartaric acid.

rows.stem:
The water of crystallization is present in

(i) Bleaching Powder

(ii) Plaster of Paris

(iii) Washing Soda

(iv) Baking Soda
rows.solution:
Plaster of Paris is \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O}\) and washing soda is \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\); both contain water of crystallisation. Bleaching powder (\(\mathrm{CaOCl_2}\)) and baking soda (\(\mathrm{NaHCO_3}\)) do not.

This is option (B) (ii) and (iii).

rows.stem: A tall pea plant with round seeds (TTRR) is crossed with a short pea plant with wrinkled seeds (ttrr). The \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation will be
rows.solution:
TTRR gives gametes TR and ttrr gives gametes tr, so every \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plant is TtRr. Tall and round are dominant, so all the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are tall with round seeds.

This is option (D) 100% tall with round seeds.

rows.stem: A pair of endocrine glands located in the human brain is
rows.solution:
The hypothalamus and the pineal gland both lie in the brain. (The thymus is in the chest and the parathyroids are in the neck.)

This is option (D) Hypothalamus and Pineal.

rows.stem:
Select the option having correct matching of the organism given in Column I with the mode of reproduction in Column II :

| Column I | Column II |
|---|---|
| P Leishmania | 1. Regeneration |
| Q Spirogyra | 2. Multiple Fission |
| R Planaria | 3. Binary Fission |
| S Plasmodium | 4. Fragmentation |
|  | 5. Budding |
rows.solution:
*Leishmania* reproduces by binary fission, *Spirogyra* by fragmentation, *Planaria* by regeneration and *Plasmodium* by multiple fission.

So P-3, Q-4, R-1, S-2, which is option (C).

rows.stem: The basic filtration unit of the excretory system in human beings is :
rows.solution: Each kidney contains a large number of nephrons, the basic filtering units that form urine from the blood. This is option (A) Nephron.

rows.stem: In human alimentary canal, the digestive juice secreted by the gastric glands are
rows.solution:
The gastric glands in the stomach wall release hydrochloric acid, the protein-digesting enzyme pepsin and mucus. (Bile comes from the liver, trypsin and lipase from the pancreas, and salivary amylase from the salivary glands.)

This is option (B) Hydrochloric acid, Pepsin, Mucus.

rows.stem: Identify from the following the ray diagram which shows the correct path of the reflected ray for the ray incident on a concave mirror as shown :

options.label: A
options.text: Diagram (A) as printed - a ray diagram of the reflected ray from the concave mirror; see the attached figure.

options.label: B
options.text: Diagram (B) as printed - a ray diagram of the reflected ray from the concave mirror; see the attached figure.

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram (C) as printed - a ray diagram of the reflected ray from the concave mirror; see the attached figure.

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram (D) as printed - a ray diagram of the reflected ray from the concave mirror; see the attached figure.

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the stem shows a ray incident on a concave mirror (principal axis with C, F and pole P marked) and all four options are drawn ray diagrams of the reflected ray; the options ARE the figure, and the path each draws is withheld here. Page idx 10.
rows.solution: A ray parallel to the principal axis, after reflection from a concave mirror, passes through the principal focus F. The diagram that shows the reflected ray passing through F is option (C).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: The part of human eye which controls the amount of light entering into it.
rows.solution:
The iris adjusts the size of the pupil, and the pupil is the opening through which light enters. NCERT states that the pupil regulates and controls the amount of light entering the eye, and the marking scheme follows it. (The iris, which changes the size of the pupil, can also be argued.)

The marking scheme's answer is option (D) Pupil.

rows.stem:
Consider the following food chain :

Grass \(\rightarrow\) Grasshopper \(\rightarrow\) Frog \(\rightarrow\) Snake \(\rightarrow\) Eagle

If the amount of energy available at third trophic level is 50 kJ, the available energy at the producer level was :
rows.solution:
Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next. Grass is the first level and the frog the third, so the energy is multiplied by 10 twice going back to the producers:

\(50 \times 10 \times 10 = 5000\) kJ, which is option (D) 5000 kJ.

rows.stem: The **incorrect** statement about ozone is

options.label: A
options.text: It is a deadly poisonous gas.

options.label: B
options.text: It shields the surface of the earth from UV radiation from sun.

options.label: C
options.text: It is used as a refrigerant and in fire-extinguishers.

options.label: D
options.text: It is formed by combining oxygen molecule with free oxygen atom.

rows.solution:
Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), not ozone, are used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers; they are what deplete the ozone layer. The other statements about ozone are true.

The incorrect statement is option (C) It is used as a refrigerant and in fire-extinguishers.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Carbon and its compounds are our major sources of fuels.

**Reason (R) :** Most of the carbon compounds on burning release a large amount of heat and light.
rows.context: Q. Nos. 17 to 20, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Carbon and its compounds (coal, petroleum, natural gas, wood) are our main fuels, so the Assertion is true. They are used as fuels because most of them burn releasing a large amount of heat and light, so the Reason is true and explains the Assertion.

This is option (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Xylem tissue moves water and minerals obtained from the soil by the roots.

**Reason (R) :** Xylem tissue is found only in the roots of a plant.
rows.context: Q. Nos. 17 to 20, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Xylem carries water and minerals absorbed from the soil by the roots, so the Assertion is true. But xylem is found in the roots, stems and leaves, not only in the roots, so the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** In the common domestic circuits the earth wire is connected to a metallic plate buried deep inside the earth.

**Reason (R) :** Earth wire ensures that any leakage of current to the metallic body of the appliance keeps its potential to that of the earth, so the user may not get a severe electric shock.
rows.context: Q. Nos. 17 to 20, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
In domestic circuits the earth wire is connected to a metal plate buried deep in the earth, so the Assertion is true. This is done so that any current leaking to the metal body of an appliance keeps its potential at that of the earth, and the user does not get a severe shock. The Reason is true and explains the Assertion.

This is option (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Food web is a network of several food chains operating in an ecosystem.

**Reason (R) :** Food web decreases the stability of an ecosystem.
rows.context: Q. Nos. 17 to 20, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
A food web is a network of many food chains in an ecosystem, so the Assertion is true. A food web gives each organism several sources of food, which increases the stability of the ecosystem, so the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
A light green coloured solution of sulphate salt of metal ‘P’ is taken in a beaker, a rod of another metal “Q’ is put in this solution as shown the following figures :

Identify the metals ‘P’ and ‘Q’ and write its chemical equation for the reaction that occurs. State the conclusion of this reaction in terms of reactivity series of metals.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - two beakers, each with a rod of metal Q in a solution, joined by an arrow 'After about 1 hour'; the labels 'PSO4 (Light Green Solution)' and 'QSO4 (Colourless Solution)' exist only in the drawing, and the colourless product is the clue the question turns on. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
The light green solution is iron(II) sulphate, so P is iron (Fe). The solution becomes colourless, so the metal Q has displaced iron and formed a colourless sulphate: Q is zinc (or magnesium).

\(\mathrm{FeSO_4 + Zn \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + Fe}\) (or \(\mathrm{FeSO_4 + Mg \rightarrow MgSO_4 + Fe}\))

Conclusion: a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution, so Q (zinc or magnesium) is more reactive than iron and lies above it in the reactivity series.

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem:
(a) How is brain protected in our body ?

(b) A doctor finds in one of his patients that he is not maintaining a proper posture and balance of his body. State the region of brain and also the part of brain which is responsible for it.
rows.solution:
(a) The brain lies inside a bony box, the skull (cranium). Inside it, the brain is held in a fluid-filled balloon that absorbs shocks.

(b) Posture and balance are controlled by the cerebellum, which is a part of the hind-brain.

rows.stem: “Proteins control the expression of various characters.” Explain this statement by taking an example of “tallness” as a characteristic in plants.
rows.solution: A gene carries the information for making a particular protein. The height of a plant depends on the amount of a particular plant hormone, and the hormone is made with the help of an enzyme, which is a protein. If the gene gives an efficient enzyme, a lot of hormone is made and the plant is tall; if the enzyme is less efficient, less hormone is made and the plant is short. So the protein made by the gene controls the character.

rows.stem: Explain the mechanism of inheritance used by sexually reproducing organisms to ensure the stability of DNA of the species.
rows.solution: Each body cell has two copies of every chromosome, one from each parent. When gametes form, each gamete receives only one chromosome of each pair, so it has half the normal number. When a male gamete and a female gamete fuse at fertilisation, the normal number of chromosomes is restored in the offspring. In this way the amount of DNA stays the same from generation to generation, ensuring the stability of the DNA of the species.

rows.stem:
Study the figure in which the path of a ray of light going from Medium 1 to Medium 2 is shown.

(a) Out of the two Media – Medium 1 and Medium 2, in which is the speed of light more ?

(b) State reason of bending of the refracted ray away from the normal.

(c) Express refractive index of Medium 2 with respect to Medium 1 in terms of speed of light in two media.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a boxed drawing of an incident ray in Medium 1 meeting the boundary with Medium 2, a dashed normal and the refracted ray; the stem's part (b) names the bending, but (a) and (c) are posed on the drawing. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(a) The refracted ray bends away from the normal, so the light speeds up as it enters medium 2. The speed of light is more in medium 2.

(b) The ray bends away from the normal because it travels from an optically denser medium (medium 1) into an optically rarer medium (medium 2), where light travels faster.

(c) \(n_{21} = \dfrac{\text{speed of light in medium 1}}{\text{speed of light in medium 2}}\).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
Give reasons :

(i) The sky appears dark to passengers flying at very high altitude.

(ii) ‘Danger’ signal lights are red in colour.
rows.solution:
(i) At very high altitudes there is hardly any air, so there are almost no particles to scatter sunlight. With no scattering, the sky looks dark.

(ii) Red light has the longest wavelength and is scattered the least by fog or smoke. So red light can be seen from a large distance, and danger signals use it.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: What is a rainbow ? “We see a rainbow in the sky only after the rainfall.” Why ?
rows.solution:
A rainbow is a natural spectrum that appears in the sky after a rain shower.

It is seen only after rainfall because it needs tiny water droplets in the air. Each droplet acts like a small prism: sunlight entering it is refracted and dispersed into its colours, reflected inside the drop, and refracted again as it leaves. Without the droplets this cannot happen.

rows.stem: We do not clean natural ponds or lakes whereas an aquarium or a swimming pool needs to be cleaned regularly. Why ?
rows.solution: Ponds and lakes are natural ecosystems with decomposers, such as bacteria and fungi, that break down dead matter and waste and keep the water clean. An aquarium or a swimming pool is a man-made ecosystem without such decomposers, so its waste keeps building up and would harm the fishes and plants (or the swimmers). It must therefore be cleaned regularly.

rows.stem:
Write balanced chemical equation for the reactions that occur when

(a) steam is passed over red hot iron.

(b) natural gas is burnt in air.

(c) glucose reacts with oxygen in the cells of our body and provides energy.
rows.solution:
(a) \(\mathrm{3Fe(s) + 4H_2O(g) \rightarrow Fe_3O_4(s) + 4H_2(g)}\)

(b) \(\mathrm{CH_4 + 2O_2 \rightarrow CO_2 + 2H_2O}\) (+ heat and light)

(c) \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \rightarrow 6CO_2 + 6H_2O}\) + energy

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem:
State the chemical property in each case on which the following uses of baking soda are based upon :

(i) as an anti-acids

(ii) as a constituent in making baking powder

(iii) in soda-acid fire-extinguishers
rows.solution:
(i) Baking soda is a mild, non-corrosive basic salt, so as an antacid it neutralises the excess acid in the stomach.

(ii) In baking powder, baking soda reacts with a mild edible acid (such as tartaric acid) to give carbon dioxide, which makes the dough rise and the cake soft and spongy.

(iii) In a soda-acid fire extinguisher, baking soda reacts with an acid (sulphuric acid) to give carbon dioxide, which puts out the fire.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem:
Write chemical equations to show what happens when an acid reacts with a

(i) metal

(ii) base and

(iii) carbonate

Write the name of the main product formed in each case.
rows.solution:
(i) Acid and metal give a salt and hydrogen:

\(\mathrm{Zn + 2HCl \rightarrow ZnCl_2 + H_2}\); main product zinc chloride.

(ii) Acid and base give a salt and water (neutralisation):

\(\mathrm{2NaOH + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + 2H_2O}\); main product sodium sulphate.

(iii) Acid and carbonate give a salt, water and carbon dioxide:

\(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 + 2HCl \rightarrow 2NaCl + H_2O + CO_2}\); main product sodium chloride.

rows.stem: Name the blood vessel that brings (i) oxygenated blood (ii) deoxygenated blood, to the human heart. Also name that chamber of the heart which receives deoxygenated blood and state how deoxygenated blood from this chamber is sent to lungs for oxygenation.
rows.solution:
(i) The pulmonary vein brings oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.

(ii) The vena cava brings deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart.

Deoxygenated blood is received by the right atrium. When the right atrium contracts, the blood passes into the right ventricle. The right ventricle then contracts and pumps the blood through the pulmonary artery to the lungs for oxygenation.

rows.stem:
The gene combination of purple flowered pea plants is denoted as (WW) and that of white flowered pea plants as (ww), when these two plants are crossed \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation is obtained.

(a) List two observations made by Mendel in \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation plants.

(b) Give the (i) percentage of white flowered plants and (ii) ratio of the gene combinations WW, Ww and ww in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation.

(c) Write one difference between dominant and recessive trait.
rows.solution:
(a) Any two: all the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants had purple flowers; there were no white-flowered plants; there were no plants with mixed (intermediate) colour; only the dominant trait of one parent appeared.

(b) Crossing the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants (\(\mathrm{Ww} \times \mathrm{Ww}\)) gives WW : Ww : ww = 1 : 2 : 1.

(i) White-flowered plants (ww) are 25%.

(ii) The ratio WW : Ww : ww is 1 : 2 : 1.

(c) A dominant trait shows itself even when the contrasting trait is also present; a recessive trait stays hidden in the presence of its contrasting (dominant) form.

rows.stem:
A student placed a candle flame at different distances from a convex lens and focused its image on a screen. He recorded his observation in tabular form as given below :

| S.No. | Distance of flame from the lens (cm) | Distance of the image from the lens |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | \(-90\) | \(+18\) |
| 2 | \(-60\) | \(+20\) |
| 3 | \(-40\) | \(+24\) |
| 4 | \(-30\) | \(+30\) |
| 5 | \(-24\) | \(+40\) |
| 6 | \(-20\) | \(+60\) |
| 7 | \(-18\) | \(+90\) |
| 8 | \(-12\) | \(+120\) |

Analyse the observation table and on the basis of your analysis only, answer the following questions (without doing any calculations) :

(a) What is the focal length of the convex lens used ? Give reason to justify your answer.

(b) Which one of the sets of observations is *not* correct and why ?

(c) Draw ray diagram to show image formation for any correct set of observation.
rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: says the image distance in observation 8 should be \(-120\) cm; for \(u = -12\) cm and \(f = 15\) cm the lens formula gives \(v = -60\) cm. Its point, that the image must be virtual and on the object's side, is unaffected.]

(a) In observation 4 the object and the image are both 30 cm from the lens. For a convex lens this happens only when the object is at 2F, so \(2f = 30\) cm and the focal length is +15 cm.

(b) Observation 8 is not correct. There the object (12 cm) is between the optical centre and the focus (15 cm), so the image is virtual and on the same side as the object; it cannot be on a screen at +120 cm. The image distance should be negative.

(c) Ray diagram for observation 4 (object at 2F): from the top of the object draw a ray parallel to the axis, which after refraction passes through \(\mathrm{F_2}\), and a ray through the optical centre, which goes straight on. They meet at \(2\mathrm{F_2}\) below the axis: the image is real, inverted and the same size as the object. (A diagram for any other correct observation is equally acceptable.)

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem:
A person uses lenses of \(+2.0\) D power in his spectacles for the correction of his vision.

(a) Name the defect of vision the person is suffering from.

(b) List two causes of this defect.

(c) Determine the focal length of the lenses used in the spectacles.
rows.solution:
(a) A +2.0 D lens is convex, used to correct hypermetropia (far-sightedness).

(b) The eyeball has become too small, or the focal length of the eye lens is too long (the lens has become less converging).

(c) \(f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{2{\cdot}0} = +0{\cdot}5\) m (50 cm).

rows.stem:
(a) Explain the statement “Potential difference between two points is 1 volt”.

(b) What do the symbols given below represent in an electric circuit ? Write one function of each.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - part (b) asks what two printed circuit symbols, labelled (i) and (ii), represent; the symbols exist only in the drawing and naming them would state the answer, so they are not described. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
(a) It means that 1 joule of work is done to move a charge of 1 coulomb from one point to the other.

(b) (i) An ammeter: it measures the electric current in a circuit.

(ii) A rheostat (variable resistance): it is used to change the resistance, and so the current, in a circuit.

rows.stem: Name an alcohol and a carboxylic acid having two carbon atoms in their structures. Draw their structures and state how this alcohol can be converted into a carboxylic acid. What happens when these two compounds react in the presence of an acid ? Write chemical equations for the reactions involved in the two cases mentioned above.
rows.solution:
The alcohol is ethanol, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}\), and the acid is ethanoic acid, \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\).

Structures: ethanol is two carbon atoms joined by a single bond, the first carrying three hydrogens and the second two hydrogens and an –OH group. Ethanoic acid is a carbon carrying three hydrogens joined to a carbon that carries a double-bonded oxygen and an –OH group.

Ethanol is converted to ethanoic acid by oxidation with alkaline potassium permanganate (or acidified potassium dichromate) on heating:

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{alkaline } KMnO_4,\ \text{heat}} CH_3COOH}\)

When ethanol and ethanoic acid react in the presence of an acid, an ester (ethyl ethanoate) is formed:

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH + CH_3COOH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O}\)

rows.stem: What are soaps ? Write the structure of a soap molecule. Explain the cleansing action of a soap. Why are soaps not considered suitable for washing clothes in a region where water is hard ? How is this problem overcomed ?
rows.solution:
Soaps are the sodium or potassium salts of long-chain carboxylic acids.

A soap molecule has two ends: an ionic end (\(\mathrm{-COO^-Na^+}\)) that is hydrophilic (attracted to water) and a long hydrocarbon chain that is hydrophobic (attracted to oil).

Cleansing action: most dirt is oily and does not dissolve in water. In soapy water the hydrocarbon tails dissolve in the oil while the ionic heads stay in the water, so the molecules gather round the dirt in clusters called micelles, with the oil trapped in the centre. This forms an emulsion, and the dirt is washed away with the water.

Hard water contains calcium and magnesium salts, which react with soap to form an insoluble scum, so little lather forms and soap is wasted. The problem is overcome by using detergents, which lather even in hard water (or by removing the hardness of the water).

rows.stem:
(a) Define Puberty. List any two changes seen in boys at the time of puberty.

(b) Why are testes in human males located outside the abdominal cavity in scrotum ?

(c) List any three techniques of contraception used by humans. Which one of these is **not** meant for males ?
rows.solution:
(a) Puberty is the period of adolescence when general body growth slows down and the reproductive tissues begin to mature.

Changes in boys (any two): the voice cracks and deepens; thick hair grows on the face; hair grows in the armpits and genital area; the penis occasionally enlarges and becomes erect.

(b) Sperm formation needs a temperature lower than the normal body temperature, so the testes lie outside the abdominal cavity, in the scrotum.

(c) Any three: mechanical barriers such as condoms; chemical methods such as oral pills; a loop or copper-T placed in the uterus; surgical methods (blocking the vas deferens or the fallopian tube).

Oral pills and the loop or copper-T are not meant for males.

rows.stem:
(a) Name the part performing following functions in human female reproductive system :

(i) production of eggs

(ii) site of fertilization

(iii) site of implantation

(iv) entry of the sperms

(b) What changes are observed in the uterus :

(i) subsequent to implantation of zygote and

(ii) if an egg does not get fertilized ?
rows.solution:
(a) (i) Production of eggs: ovary. (ii) Site of fertilisation: oviduct (fallopian tube). (iii) Site of implantation: uterus. (iv) Entry of sperms: vagina.

(b) (i) After implantation, the zygote keeps dividing in the uterus. The thickened, blood-rich lining of the uterus nourishes the embryo, and a placenta develops, which supplies oxygen and food to the embryo and removes its wastes.

(ii) If the egg is not fertilised, the thick lining of the uterus is not needed. It slowly breaks down and comes out through the vagina as blood and mucus, along with the unfertilised egg (menstruation).

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem:
What are magnetic field lines ? How is the direction of magnetic field at a point determined ? Draw the pattern of magnetic field lines of the magnetic field produced by a current carrying circular loop. Mark on it the direction of (i) current and (ii) magnetic field lines.

Name the two factors on which the magnitude of the magnetic field due to a current carrying coil depends.
rows.solution:
Magnetic field lines are the imaginary lines around a magnet along which a north pole would move; together they show the magnetic field.

The direction of the field at a point is found by placing a small compass needle there: its north pole points in the direction of the field.

Diagram: draw a circular loop with the current shown by arrows. Near each side of the wire the field lines are concentric circles around the wire; as they approach the centre of the loop they become nearly straight lines, perpendicular to the plane of the loop. Mark the direction of the current and of the field lines.

The magnitude of the field due to the coil depends on (any two): the current in it, the number of turns, and the radius of the coil.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem:
Why can’t two magnetic field lines cross each other ? Draw magnetic field lines showing the direction of the magnetic field due to a current carrying long straight solenoid. State the conclusion which can be drawn from the pattern of magnetic field lines inside the solenoid.

Name any two factors on which the magnitude of the magnetic field due to this solenoid depends.
rows.solution:
Two field lines cannot cross, because at the point of crossing the field would have two directions, and a compass needle there would have to point two ways at once, which is impossible.

Diagram: draw a solenoid connected to a cell and a key. Inside it the field lines are parallel straight lines along the axis; outside they curve round from one end to the other, like those of a bar magnet.

Conclusion: inside the solenoid the lines are parallel and equally spaced, so the magnetic field there is uniform (the same at all points).

The magnitude of the field depends on (any two): the number of turns, the current in the solenoid, and the material of the core inside it.

rows.stem: How does electrical conductivity and melting point of a metal change when it is converted to its alloy by mixing a small amount of an element in it ?
rows.context: Many pure metals like copper, iron and gold are very soft and as such are considered unsuitable for certain uses. Metallic objects around us such as cooking utensils, statues, ornaments, guns etc. are actually not made up of pure metals. Instead of pure metals, alloys are used in the design of most of the useful objects. Making alloys enhances the basic properties of a metal which is the primary constituent (metal) of an alloy.
rows.solution: When a pure metal is made into an alloy, both its electrical conductivity and its melting point become lower than those of the pure metal. (In a few cases the melting point can rise.)

rows.stem: Name an alloy used for welding two wires together in an electric circuit. Write its major constituents.
rows.context: Many pure metals like copper, iron and gold are very soft and as such are considered unsuitable for certain uses. Metallic objects around us such as cooking utensils, statues, ornaments, guns etc. are actually not made up of pure metals. Instead of pure metals, alloys are used in the design of most of the useful objects. Making alloys enhances the basic properties of a metal which is the primary constituent (metal) of an alloy.
rows.solution: Solder, an alloy of lead (Pb) and tin (Sn), which has a low melting point.

rows.stem: What are alloys ? How is ‘Brass’ (an alloy) prepared ?
rows.context: Many pure metals like copper, iron and gold are very soft and as such are considered unsuitable for certain uses. Metallic objects around us such as cooking utensils, statues, ornaments, guns etc. are actually not made up of pure metals. Instead of pure metals, alloys are used in the design of most of the useful objects. Making alloys enhances the basic properties of a metal which is the primary constituent (metal) of an alloy.
rows.solution: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or of a metal and a non-metal. Brass is prepared by melting copper and mixing in zinc in a definite proportion, then cooling the mixture.

rows.stem: What is stainless steel ? How is it prepared ? Write one important property which makes it more useful in making cooking utensils as compared to its primary metal.
rows.context: Many pure metals like copper, iron and gold are very soft and as such are considered unsuitable for certain uses. Metallic objects around us such as cooking utensils, statues, ornaments, guns etc. are actually not made up of pure metals. Instead of pure metals, alloys are used in the design of most of the useful objects. Making alloys enhances the basic properties of a metal which is the primary constituent (metal) of an alloy.
rows.solution:
Stainless steel is an alloy of iron (steel) with nickel and chromium. Iron is first mixed with a small amount of carbon (about 0.05%), which makes it hard and strong, and then nickel and chromium are added.

It does not rust, which makes it better than pure iron for cooking utensils.

rows.stem: Name the movement which causes ‘X’ and ‘Y’ to grow downwards and upwards respectively. (Refer above figure)
rows.context: The growth movements of plant parts in which the direction of the stimulus determines the direction of the response is known as tropic movements or tropism. Plants also have non-directional movements which may not be growth dependent.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a potted plant lying on its side, its roots labelled X and its shoot labelled Y; the stem says '(Refer above figure)' and the labels X and Y are defined only in the drawing. Page idx 28.
rows.solution: X (the roots) grows downwards, towards gravity: positive geotropism. Y (the shoot) grows upwards, away from gravity: negative geotropism. (These are also described as negative and positive phototropism respectively.)

rows.stem: Write the name of a hormone that plays a major role in (i) falling of leaves (ii) rapid cell division
rows.context: The growth movements of plant parts in which the direction of the stimulus determines the direction of the response is known as tropic movements or tropism. Plants also have non-directional movements which may not be growth dependent.
rows.solution:
(i) Falling of leaves: abscisic acid.

(ii) Rapid cell division: cytokinin.

rows.stem: Leaves of the sensitive plant move very quickly in response to ‘touch’. How is this stimulus of touch communicated and explain how the movement takes place.
rows.context: The growth movements of plant parts in which the direction of the stimulus determines the direction of the response is known as tropic movements or tropism. Plants also have non-directional movements which may not be growth dependent.
rows.solution: The touch is communicated from cell to cell by electrical-chemical means, since plants have no nerves. The cells then change shape by changing the amount of water in them: they shrink or swell, and this makes the leaves fold.

rows.stem: Name the plant hormone which is synthesized at the shoot tip. How does this hormone helps the plant to bend towards light ?
rows.context: The growth movements of plant parts in which the direction of the stimulus determines the direction of the response is known as tropic movements or tropism. Plants also have non-directional movements which may not be growth dependent.
rows.solution:
Auxin is made at the shoot tip.

When light comes from one side, auxin diffuses towards the shaded side of the shoot. The higher concentration of auxin makes the cells on the shaded side grow longer, so the shoot bends towards the light.

rows.stem: Draw a circuit diagram showing the above two resistors X and Y joined in parallel with same battery and same ammeter and voltmeter.
rows.context: Study the circuit shown in which two resistors X and Y of resistances \(3\,\Omega\) and \(6\,\Omega\) respectively are joined in series with a battery of 2 V.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit (X = 3 Ω and Y = 6 Ω in series, a voltmeter V across the pair, an ammeter A, a 2 V battery and a plug key, with meter polarities marked) is given only as a drawing, and (I) asks to redraw it with the same battery, ammeter and voltmeter. Page idx 30.
rows.solution: Connect X (\(3\,\Omega\)) and Y (\(6\,\Omega\)) in parallel between two points. Connect the voltmeter across this parallel pair, and connect the ammeter, the 2 V battery and the plug key in series with the pair. The positive terminal of each meter goes towards the positive terminal of the battery.

rows.stem: In which combination of resistors will the (i) potential difference across X and Y and (ii) current through X and Y, be the same ?
rows.context: Study the circuit shown in which two resistors X and Y of resistances \(3\,\Omega\) and \(6\,\Omega\) respectively are joined in series with a battery of 2 V.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the shared series circuit of this case study; the values needed are in the passage. Page idx 30.
rows.solution:
(i) The potential difference across X and Y is the same in the parallel combination.

(ii) The current through X and Y is the same in the series combination.

rows.stem: Find the current drawn from the battery by the series combination of the two resistors (X and Y).
rows.context: Study the circuit shown in which two resistors X and Y of resistances \(3\,\Omega\) and \(6\,\Omega\) respectively are joined in series with a battery of 2 V.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the shared series circuit of this case study; the values needed are in the passage. Page idx 30.
rows.solution:
In series, \(R = 3 + 6 = 9\,\Omega\).

\(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{2}{9} \approx 0{\cdot}22\) A.

rows.stem: Determine the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination of the two resistors (X and Y).
rows.context: Study the circuit shown in which two resistors X and Y of resistances \(3\,\Omega\) and \(6\,\Omega\) respectively are joined in series with a battery of 2 V.
